clue.text: Old Chinese mother acting dumb?

parts.note: mum is an everyday word for a mother
the Ming dynasty ruled China from 1368 to 1644, so Ming suggests old Chinese porcelain or rule

explanation.surface: A question about whether an elderly Chinese mother is struck dumb.
explanation.walkthrough: Mumming is performing in a traditional mummers' play, a largely wordless masked show, hence the question mark on 'acting dumb'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mummers traditionally performed silent masked plays, so the activity is a kind of dumb-show performing.

clue.text: Twist, note — and with little hesitation!

parts.note: me (or mi) is the third note of the sol-fa scale
er is the sound of a brief hesitation in speech

explanation.surface: Someone twisting and making a note, with a brief pause.
explanation.definitionFit: A river that winds back and forth twists along its course.

clue.text: An eminent artist may have set aims

indicators.note: may have hints that the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A great painter might well have set himself goals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may have' signals rearranging SETAIMS, the letters of 'set aims'.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Matisse was a leading French painter of the Fauvist movement.

clue.text: Only some of the dinner-ladies will be on target

indicators.note: only some of the letters in these words are used, a run hidden inside them

explanation.surface: Just a few of the school dinner-ladies will hit the mark.
explanation.walkthrough: Dinner-ladies are school canteen staff in Britain. The 'on target' sense is the ring just outside the bull on a dartboard or archery target.
explanation.definitionFit: On an archery or rifle target, the ring next to the bull is a scoring zone.

clue.text: Bombastic, though ill-organised

indicators.note: ill in the sense of badly done, so the letters of organised are messed up

explanation.surface: A pompous plan, even though it is badly put together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'though' is a link; 'ill' says the letters of 'organised' are badly ordered.
explanation.definitionFit: Pompous or overblown language is showy and inflated, just like a bombastic manner.

clue.text: Meals to take out

parts.note: reads like a takeaway order, but means food carried outdoors to eat in the open air

explanation.definitionFit: Outdoor meals packed up and eaten in a park or field are taken out of the house.

clue.text: A bird — it's after seed

indicators.note: after means it comes behind the seed word

parts.note: a pip is a fruit seed
it, the word itself

explanation.surface: A bird is after some seed.
explanation.definitionFit: A small brown songbird of open country, related to wagtails.

clue.text: Many stick around a ship and row back for recreation

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many

indicators.note: the stick goes around the ship and the other word

parts.note: a rod is a stick
SS stands for steamship

indicators.note: back means the word row is read in reverse

explanation.surface: Lots of people paddle round a boat and row home for fun.
explanation.definitionFit: A word puzzle solved for pleasure is a pastime.

clue.text: Gather a small number raise hell

parts.note: to gather is to infer or deduce
no is a short form of number

explanation.surface: A crowd gathering few people decides to raise hell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raise' is a link here; the definition is just 'hell'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dante's poem names the underworld of fire, so a blazing hell is an infernal place.

clue.text: Alcoholic drink is for the non-driver

definitions.meaning: a cocktail of brandy, orange liqueur and lemon juice
the passenger compartment attached to a motorcycle

explanation.definitionFit: A brandy cocktail has this name, and the attached passenger car on a motorbike carries the person who is not riding.

clue.text: A woman should receive a number, one feels

indicators.note: the woman's name takes in the number, which goes into the middle of it

parts.note: Anna is a woman's name
ten is a number

explanation.surface: Advice that a woman ought to be given a number.
explanation.definitionFit: An insect's feeler is the organ it uses to sense its surroundings by touch.

clue.text: Parking under cover, protected from inclement weather

parts.note: P is the standard abbreviation for parking on road signs
a building under cover has a roof over it, i.e. it is roofed

explanation.surface: A car park with a roof keeps vehicles safe from bad weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Weatherproofed material has been treated so rain and wind cannot get through.

clue.text: Record concerning daughter-it will bring censure

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
re means concerning or about, as in business letters
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A record about a daughter will lead to her being blamed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will' is a link; to discredit someone is to bring censure or disgrace upon them.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring someone into disrepute is to damage their good name, the effect of public reproach.

clue.text: Stresses retreating glacial ice

indicators.note: something retreating goes backwards, so the word for stresses is read in reverse

parts.note: cares are worries or stresses

explanation.surface: Worries receding, like ice withdrawing on a glacier.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinnacle or ridge of ice formed where a glacier's surface breaks up into crevasses.

clue.text: Thin and awfully dry around mid-week

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the middle of the week
awfully suggests something badly done, so the letters of dry are jumbled
mid- picks the middle letters of the word week

explanation.surface: A complaint that the middle of the week has been thin and very dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' turns DRY into RDY, which goes 'around' EE, the middle two letters of 'week'.
explanation.definitionFit: A reedy voice or figure is slender and weak, like a reed's stalk.

clue.text: The standard detectives adhere to

parts.note: the Yard is Scotland Yard, London's police headquarters
to stick is to adhere

explanation.surface: The rule that detectives follow.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotland Yard is the headquarters of London's Metropolitan Police, so 'the Yard' means its detectives.
explanation.definitionFit: A measure against which others are judged is a benchmark.

clue.text: Not at all well 23 down?

definitions.meaning: slightly ill or out of sorts
the solution at 23 down is a colour, and someone looking sickly is said to have turned that colour

explanation.definitionFit: Being slightly ill makes a person look pale, and someone looking green about the gills is unwell.

clue.text: Fans get in, smashing the security device

indicators.note: smashing breaks the letters up to be reformed

explanation.surface: Football fans break in by smashing the lock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smashing' shuffles FANSGETIN, the letters of 'Fans get in'.
explanation.definitionFit: A clasp, lock or bolt is a device that secures something shut.

clue.text: Enthusiasm is shown as new gear's seen

indicators.note: new suggests the letters are made over in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Excitement shows when someone unveils new equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' tells you to rearrange GEARSSEEN, the letters of 'gear's seen'.
explanation.definitionFit: Keenness or eagerness is the eager desire that enthusiasm expresses.

clue.text: He brought out the earlier model

parts.note: ex means former or earlier, as in ex-wife
a poser is someone who poses, as a model does

explanation.surface: He launched the previous version of the product.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who reveals or uncovers something brings it out into the open.

clue.text: Fish to catch from deck

parts.note: a gar is a long-snouted fish
to land a fish is to catch it

explanation.surface: Hauling a fish up from the deck of a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deck' looks like a ship's deck but is a verb, to adorn; 'to' and 'from' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To decorate with flowers is to deck or adorn, as with a wreath.

clue.text: Clips non-ornamental plants

definitions.meaning: to clip or cut short, as a tail or wages
broad-leaved weeds of the sorrel family, plants nobody grows for show

explanation.definitionFit: To cut short a tail is to curtail it, and the weed family Rumex includes common wild sorrels.

clue.text: A miner's dog Rex

parts.note: a collie is a breed of sheepdog
R stands for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A miner owns a dog called Rex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rex' looks like a dog's name but is the king, R, as in royal signatures.
explanation.definitionFit: A coal worker toils underground, digging seams of coal.

clue.text: Recalcitrant lads can cause 11

indicators.note: unruly behaviour suggests the letters will not stay in order

explanation.surface: Unruly boys can bring disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalcitrant' jumbles LADSCAN, from 'lads can'; 11 across is DISCREDIT, which a public outrage brings.
explanation.definitionFit: A public outrage brings disgrace and damage to reputations.

clue.text: Equality is capital!

parts.note: par means equality, as in 'on a par'

explanation.surface: An exclamation that equality is excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' doubles as old-fashioned slang for excellent, but here means a capital city, the French one.
explanation.definitionFit: The French capital city is the seat of government of France.

clue.text: Irregular, irregular, endlessly irregular cash-holding

indicators.note: the jumbled letters hold the cash letter inside them
the second irregular says the letters that follow are put in an irregular order
endlessly drops the last letter of the third irregular

parts.note: L stands for pounds sterling, a sum of cash

explanation.surface: A repetitive complaint about some highly irregular handling of money.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'irregular' is the definition, a guerrilla being an irregular soldier; 'endlessly' trims the third to IRREGULA, 'irregular' scrambles it, and 'holding' puts L inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A guerrilla fights in an unofficial band rather than a regular army, so is an irregular soldier.

clue.text: Inexperienced environmentalist

definitions.meaning: a campaigner for the environment, especially a member of an ecology party

explanation.definitionFit: A raw novice is unripe like young growth, and ecology campaigners take the colour of leaves as their emblem.

clue.text: Tear over a place in Northern England

parts.note: to rip is to tear
on can mean over, as in on top of

explanation.surface: A rip on a trip to a northern town.
explanation.walkthrough: Ripon is a small cathedral city in North Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathedral city in North Yorkshire.

clue.text: A resort area that sets the South-east apart

parts.note: SE is the compass abbreviation for south-east
aside means apart, as in setting something aside

explanation.surface: A holiday resort that marks out England's south-east coast as special.
explanation.definitionFit: A coastal holiday town is the kind of resort people visit beside the sea.

clue.text: The rascal was untruthful and made insinuations

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous rascal
lied means was untruthful

explanation.surface: A mischievous child told lies and dropped sly hints.
explanation.definitionFit: To suggest something without saying it outright is to hint or insinuate.

clue.text: Brave maybe-relative to revolutionaries, that is!

parts.note: Reds are communists or revolutionaries
kin are relatives

explanation.surface: A brave fellow who turns out to be related to revolutionaries.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'brave' here is a Native American warrior, the old (now offensive) term the answer gives; 'maybe' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Dated and now offensive term for a Native American, and a warrior of such a people was called a brave.

clue.text: Common sorts left behind

parts.note: genera are sorts or kinds, the plural of genus

explanation.surface: Ordinary types left at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' places L at the end of GENERA.
explanation.definitionFit: Something widespread or shared by most is common rather than particular.
